Customers are blood centres and hospitals in the US, Europe and elsewhere, and revenue is around 150 to 200 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (CERS) and headquartered in Concord, California. Known to transfusion medicine specialists, with no general consumer awareness.

Circle Pharma is a US biotechnology company developing macrocycle drugs, a class of cyclic peptide-like molecules, aimed at cancer targets that are hard to reach, notably cell-cycle (cyclin) inhibitors, with candidate CID-078. It is private and venture backed, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It has no approved products and no consumer awareness, and is known only to investors and oncology specialists, so it has little sponsorship relevance.

CREATE Medicines is a US biotechnology company, formerly Myeloid Therapeutics, developing in vivo CAR therapies, using mRNA delivered to patients to program their own immune cells to fight cancer and autoimmune disease, without cell manufacturing outside the body. about: Curis is a US biotechnology company that discovered Erivedge (vismodegib), a hedgehog pathway inhibitor for advanced basal cell carcinoma marketed by Roche/Genentech, from which it earns royalties, and now develops oncology candidates such as emavusertib for blood cancers. It has no major product revenue of its own. Listed on Nasdaq (CRIS) and based in Lexington, Massachusetts. Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Flare Therapeutics is a US biotechnology start-up developing precision medicines that target transcription factors, which control gene expression and have been hard to drug, with a first programme aimed at cancer. It was founded in 2019 with backing from Atlas Venture and others. Private and venture backed, with no approved products, no consumer awareness and no known sponsorship activity, so it is not a typical brand-sponsorship prospect.

about: GenSight Biologics is a French biotechnology company that develops gene therapy for retinal neurodegenerative diseases, led by Lumevoq (lenadogene nolparvovec) for Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, which it has distributed in France under an early access scheme. It also has optogenetic vision restoration research. Founded in 2012 and listed on Euronext Paris (SIGHT). Known to ophthalmology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Life Biosciences is a US biotechnology company developing treatments for ageing-related diseases by partially reprogramming cells to restore their youthful function, with a lead programme (ER-100) for optic neuropathies such as glaucoma and NAION. Co-founded by David Sinclair of Harvard, it is private and venture backed with no approved products. Known in longevity circles, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record.

Lycia Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company developing lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs), a way of degrading extracellular and membrane proteins, with applications in cancer and autoimmune diseases. Founded on research from Stanford University by Carolyn Bertozzi's lab, it is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and was backed by Third Rock and others. It had collaborations with Lilly and Merck. No approved products and no consumer awareness.

Median Technologies is a French medical imaging software company, offering AI-based tools for cancer imaging in clinical trials (iBiopsy) and its iCRO imaging service for drug developers, plus a lung cancer screening software in development. Customers are pharmaceutical companies and clinical research organisations, and it earns revenue from imaging core lab services. Founded in 2002 and listed on Euronext Paris (ALMDT), located in Sophia Antipolis. B2B healthcare technology brand with no consumer awareness.

MedinCell is a French pharmaceutical company that develops long-acting injectable drugs using its BEPO polymer technology, which releases a drug steadily over weeks or months. Its lead products include an injectable risperidone for schizophrenia partnered with Teva (Uzedy) and programmes in contraception, malaria and pain. Revenue comes from licensing, royalties and partner payments. Based in Montpellier and listed on Euronext Paris (MEDCL). Known to pharma partners, with no consumer awareness.

Mighty Therapeutics is a US biopharmaceutical company in Newton, Massachusetts, tagged by Crunchbase as biopharma and biotechnology. about: Nautilus Biotechnology is a US life sciences tools company developing a platform for measuring the whole proteome, the complete set of proteins in a sample, aimed at drug discovery and biomarker research customers. Known in proteomics and investor circles, with no consumer awareness.

ONWARD Medical is a Dutch-Swiss medical technology company that develops implantable and external spinal cord neurostimulation systems to restore movement in people with spinal cord injury, including the ARC-EX therapy cleared by the US FDA in 2024 and the ARC-IM and ARC-BCI platforms. Customers are rehabilitation clinics and patients. Listed on Euronext Brussels and Amsterdam (ONWD). Known in medtech and spinal injury communities, with inspiring human stories that could suit brand storytelling.

Palvella Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing QTORIN rapamycin, a topical formulation for rare skin diseases such as microcystic lymphatic malformations and pachyonychia congenita. PMV Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage precision oncology company developing drugs that target the tumour suppressor protein p53, such as rezatapopt (PC14586) for cancers with the Y220C mutation. SCYNEXIS is a US biotechnology company that developed Brexafemme (ibrexafungerp), a first-in-class oral antifungal for vaginal yeast infections and a candidate for invasive fungal diseases, licensed to GSK in 2023 for a large upfront and milestone package. Sera Prognostics is a US women's health diagnostics company that sells the PreTRM test, a blood test taken during pregnancy that estimates a woman's risk of preterm birth, based on proteomic biomarkers, and is developing further tests. Customers are obstetricians and health systems, with revenue from test sales and collaborations. Founded in 2008 and listed on Nasdaq (SERA). Shoulder Innovations is a US medical device company that develops shoulder replacement implants and instruments, including its InSet glenoid components and a pre-planning approach, aimed at orthopaedic surgeons treating shoulder arthritis. Known among orthopaedic specialists, with no consumer awareness.

Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Ray Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in the San Francisco Bay Area developing optogenetic gene therapies to restore vision in patients with retinitis pigmentosa and other inherited retinal diseases, with its lead candidate RTx-015. Known to ophthalmology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record, so it is an unlikely F1 brand partner.

Sensei Biotherapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing cancer immunotherapy, including SNS-101, an antibody targeting VISTA that is active in the acidic tumour environment. Known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record, so it is an unlikely F1 brand partner.

Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Siegfried Holding is a Swiss contract development and manufacturing organisation for pharmaceuticals, producing active pharmaceutical ingredients, intermediates and finished drug products for pharma companies at sites in Switzerland, Germany, France, Spain, Malta, the US and China. Strong B2B brand among pharma companies but unknown to consumers.

THINK Surgical is a US medical robotics company that develops the TSolution One robotic system for knee and hip replacement surgery, which uses a surgeon's 3D plan to guide an active robot that mills the bone. Based in Fremont, California, it descends from Curexo's Robodoc technology and is backed by a Korean-listed parent. Known to orthopaedic surgeons, with no consumer awareness.

TISSIUM is a French medical device company that develops biodegradable polymer-based sealants and tissue reconstruction products, with a first product, the COAPTIUM CONNECT system for nerve repair, authorised by the US FDA in 2023. Customers are surgeons and hospitals. It was founded in 2013 in Paris as a spin-out from research at MIT and Harvard, and is venture backed. Known to surgeons and medtech investors, with no consumer awareness.

Triveni Bio is a US biotechnology company in Watertown, Massachusetts, developing antibody therapies for inflammatory and fibrotic diseases, especially in dermatology, such as atopic dermatitis, with candidates directed at kallikrein-related targets. Known only to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record, so it is not a typical F1 sponsorship prospect.

about: Xeltis is a Dutch clinical-stage medical technology company, based in Eindhoven, developing restorative vascular grafts and heart valves made from polymers that guide the body to grow its own tissue, with products such as the aXess vascular access graft for dialysis patients. Customers will be surgeons and hospitals once products are approved. Founded in 2010 as a spin-out of Eindhoven University of Technology and venture backed. Known to medtech specialists, with no consumer awareness.

Palo Alto blood-testing startup founded in 2003 by Elizabeth Holmes, which claimed to run hundreds of tests from a few drops of blood using its Edison devices. After a 2015 investigation by the Wall Street Journal it was shown to be fraudulent, closed in 2018, and Holmes and Ramesh Balwani were convicted of fraud. Backed by Walgreens, Safeway and investors valuing it at USD 9 billion. Defunct and infamous; a clearly toxic brand not available for sponsorship.
